FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Textile Machinery and Accessories Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textiles Division 
Council. 


A shuttle was a tool designed to neatly and compactly store a holder that carries the thread of the weft yarn while 
weaving with a loom. Shuttles are thrown or passed back and forth through the shed, between the yarn threads of 
the warp in order to weave in the weft. 


This standard was originally published in 1961 and subsequently revised in 1971. The present revision has been 
made in the light of experience gained since its publication and to incorporate the following major changes: 


a) Title of the standard has been modified; 

b) Forward has been incorporated; 

c) Scope of the standard has been incorporated; 

d) Marking clause has been modified; 

e) Packing and sampling clauses have been incorporated; and 
f) References to Indian standards have been updated. 


The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 1794 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


TEXTILES — SHUTTLES FOR PLAIN CALICO LOOMS — 
SPECIFICATION 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements of the 
shuttle used in plain calico looms. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed below contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of the standards listed below. 


IS No. Title 


IS 1141: 1993 Seasoning of timber — 
Code of practice (second 


revision) 


IS 2500 (Part 1): 2000 Sampling procedures for 
inspection by attributes: 
Part 1 Sampling schemes 
indexed by acceptance 
quality limit (AQL) for 
lot by lot inspection 
(third revision)

accessories for use in 
shuttles for plain calico 


looms 


IS 9280 : 1979 Specification for wooden 


shuttle blocks for non- 
automatic looms 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


3.1 Left-Hand Shuttle — The eye of the shuttle falls 
on the right hand side when viewed from the 
weaver's position at the front of the loom. 


3.2 Right-Hand Shuttle — The eye of the shuttle 
falls on the left hand side when viewed from the 
weaver's position at the front of the loom. 


4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 


The shape and dimensions of the shuttle are 
described in Table 1. 


5 MATERIAL 


Material used for shuttles shall be as according to 


shuttle blocks conforming to IS 9280. 
6 SHUTTLE ACCESSORIES 


Various accessories used in making shuttle shall 
preferably conform to the relevant requirements laid 
down in IS 6268. 


NOTE — H prescribed by the buyer, fibre washer shall be 
provided under the tip. 


7 WEIGHT 


The weight of a shuttle shall be as agreed to between 
the buyer and the seller subject to a tolerance of 
+ 5 percent. 


8 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 


8.1 The wood for the manufacture of shuttles shall 
be fully-seasoned (see IS 1141). 


8.2 Shuttles shall be free from knots, cracks and any 
other defect which is likely to affect the life or 
usefulness of shuttles. 


8.3 The outer surface and surfaces where the yarn 
comes in contact shall be finished smooth. 


8.4 Angle of shuttle (bevel) shall be between 84° to 
87° subject to a tolerance of + 0.5” on the angle 
prescribed by the buyer. 


NOTE — In case of shuttles intended to be used in 
conjunction with all metal reeds the angle of shuttle (bevel) 
shall normally be 90°. 


8.5 If agreed to between the buyer and the seller, 
shuttles made of uncompressed wood shall be 
impregnated with raw linseed oil. 


9 BALANCING OF SHUTTLE 


When the shuttle is held between two horizontal 
frictionless bearings (or thumb nails) so that the 
shuttle front faces the viewer the shuttle shall tilt 
towards the back. 


10 DROPPING TEST 


When the shuttle is vertically dropped with one of 
its tips facing down from a height of one metre on a 
cast iron plate the tip shall not get blunt. 


11 POSITION OF PIRN 


The pirn, when in position in a shuttle, shall lie at 
equidistance from inside opposite walls of the 
shuttle However, the difference in gap on either side 
shall not exceed 1 mm. 


IS 1794 : 2023

2 Overall length of shuttle is normally equal to length of the pirn to be accommodated plus 165 mm, Min. 


3 The height at front is normally 1 mm to 3 mm less than that at the back. 


12 MARKING 


Each shuttle shall bear the name of manufacturer or 
trade-mark, and a code number to trace the month 
and year of manufacture. 


12.1 Each shuttle for the plain calico loom shall also 
bear the following information: 


a) Type of the wood used in the shuttle; 

b) Net weight of the content; 

c) Code number to trace back the history of 
production; 

d) Hand of the shuttle whether right hand (R) 
or left hand (L); 

e) Dimension of the shuttle; 

f) Number of shuttles in lot; 

g) Gross and net mass; 

h) Lot/batch number; 


j) Country of origin; and 
k) Any other information required by the law in 
force and/or by the buyer. 


12.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
products may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


13 PACKING 


Shuttles shall be suitably packed as may be agreed 
to between the concerned parties. The package 
should contain fixed number of Shuttles essentially 
of the same variety. 


14 SAMPLING 
14.1 Lot 


In any consignment, the number of shuttles 
delivered to a buyer against a dispatch note, shall 
constitute a lot.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: TXD 14 (20115).
